correctness.rationale: Exact detailed-balance Dirichlet extension gives C_sa=pi_s p_s/alpha and C_sb=pi_s(1-p_s)/beta. Exact Gram inversion yields -V_ab=alpha(z-q)/[alpha(beta+mu)-2alpha z+q-z^2]. At fixed z, weighted Cauchy-Schwarz q>=z^2/mu and monotone quotient show the maximizer has constant p. A one-variable rational derivative gives the unique r*, and an explicit positive-conductance bipartite network attains it for every pi. Strong graph maximum principle gives the sign criterion. Rational matrix assertions verify examples, not infinitely many networks.

value.rationale: The originating RCMC method acknowledges that Type B may need a nonlinear probability-simplex correction. A universal, sharp, attained coefficient bound supplies a quantitatively meaningful failure envelope for this concrete algorithm, valid across every connected reversible graph, and exhibits unbounded amplification under rare stationary terminal weights despite projection norm one. The exact two-terminal extremal and equality construction have direct significance for detecting numerical probability invalidity; no general-time-semigroup accuracy claim is made.
